paragraphs: Some lawyers in Ireland stopped doing legal aid work in July. Now they are going back to work. The Government and the lawyers made a deal on Tuesday.
Legal aid helps people who cannot pay for a lawyer. The State pays the lawyer for them. In July, the Government changed how it pays. Many lawyers said the new pay was not fair.
Under the deal, a lawyer still gets €520 for one case. If a person has two cases on the same day, the lawyer gets €780. For three or more cases, the pay is €1,040. Long cases also get €780.
The Minister for Justice, Jim O'Callaghan, said he was very pleased. The head of the Law Society also welcomed the deal. Lawyers will start full work again on Wednesday.

paragraphs: Criminal defence solicitors in Ireland will return fully to work from Wednesday. The Department of Justice and the Law Society reached an agreement on Tuesday. It ends a long row over legal aid payments.

Legal aid means the State pays for a lawyer when a person accused of a crime cannot afford one. On 1 July, the Government brought in a new system with a single flat fee. Many solicitors said it was unfair, and they stopped taking legal aid cases for more than four months.

The new deal keeps the €520 flat fee. However, if one person has two separate cases on the same day, the solicitor will get €780. Three or more cases will pay €1,040. Long cases, such as domestic violence or children's cases, will also pay €780.
Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan said he was very pleased with the result. Law Society president Martin Lawlor said the deal fixed the two biggest problems with the system.
Earlier this month, a High Court judge said parts of the new system were very unfair. The judge has now put off her final decision until 24 November.

司法部與律師協會在星期二達成協議。
這結束了一場關於法律扶助費用的長期爭執。
法律扶助是指被控犯罪的人請不起律師時，由國家支付律師費。
七月一日，政府推出一套單一固定費用的新制度。
許多律師認為這不公平，因此四個多月來拒接法律扶助案件。
新協議保留了520歐元的固定費用。
不過，如果同一人在同一天有兩件不同的案子，律師可拿到780歐元。
三件以上的案子可拿到1,040歐元。
耗時長的案件，例如家庭暴力或兒童案件，也可拿到780歐元。
司法部長吉姆・奧卡拉漢表示對結果非常滿意。
律師協會會長馬丁・勞勒表示，這項協議解決了制度中最大的兩個問題。
本月稍早，一名高等法院法官表示新制度的部分內容非常不公平。
這位法官現在已將最終裁決延到11月24日。

paragraphs: Criminal defence solicitors are set to resume full legal aid work from Wednesday after the Department of Justice and the Law Society agreed a deal to end a dispute that had lasted more than four months.

The row began on 1 July, when Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan introduced a single flat fee of €520 per case. Under the old scheme, solicitors received €240 for a first court appearance and around €60 for each one after that. Many lawyers argued the new model was unworkable and withdrew their services.

Under the agreement, the flat fee will remain, but enhanced payments will be added. Solicitors will receive €780 when a client faces two separate cases on the same day and €1,040 for three or more. A single enhanced fee of €780 will apply to lengthy cases, including domestic violence and custody hearings.

Mr O'Callaghan said he was very pleased that his reform remained in place. Law Society president Martin Lawlor described the talks as constructive and said the deal resolved the two main flaws in the scheme.

Earlier this month, High Court judge Mary Rose Gearty ruled that key parts of the model were unfair and beyond the minister's powers. She has adjourned her final orders until 24 November, saying the matter was better settled by agreement.
sentZh: 司法部與律師協會達成協議，結束了持續四個多月的爭議，刑事辯護律師預計從星期三起全面恢復法律扶助工作。
這場爭執始於七月一日，當時司法部長吉姆・奧卡拉漢推行每案520歐元的單一固定費用。
在舊制度下，律師首次出庭可得240歐元，之後每次出庭約60歐元。
許多律師認為新模式窒礙難行，因而撤回服務。
根據協議，固定費用將保留，但會增加加給費用。
當客戶同一天面對兩件不同案件時，律師可得780歐元，三件以上則為1,040歐元。
耗時較長的案件，包括家庭暴力和羈押聆訊，將適用780歐元的單一加給費用。
奧卡拉漢表示，他很高興自己的改革得以保留。
律師協會會長馬丁・勞勒形容談判富有建設性，並說協議解決了該制度的兩大缺陷。
本月稍早，高等法院法官瑪麗・蘿絲・蓋爾蒂裁定，該模式的關鍵部分不公平且超出部長權限。
她已將最終命令延至11月24日，並表示此事最好以協議解決。

paragraphs: A protracted standoff over criminal legal aid has finally been resolved, with defence solicitors poised to return to the courts in full from Wednesday following an accord between the Department of Justice and the Law Society.

The dispute erupted in July, when Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan replaced a system of staggered payments with a single flat fee of €520 per case. Previously, solicitors earned €240 for an initial appearance and roughly €60 for each subsequent one. Branding the new arrangement unworkable, many practitioners boycotted legal aid work for over four months.

The compromise preserves the flat fee while introducing supplementary rates. Where a client faces two distinct cases on the same day, the fee rises to €780, climbing to €1,040 for three or more. Protracted matters, such as domestic violence proceedings and custody remands, will attract an enhanced fee of €780.

The minister declared himself very pleased that the core of his overhaul had survived intact. Law Society president Martin Lawlor, for his part, praised the constructive tone of the negotiations and said the deal remedied the scheme's two principal defects.

The settlement comes days after High Court judge Mary Rose Gearty found key elements of the model grossly unfair and beyond the minister's statutory powers. She has deferred her final orders until 24 November.

paragraphs: Following more than four months of disruption, criminal defence solicitors are expected to resume legal aid work in full from Wednesday, as a consequence of an agreement reached between the Department of Justice and the Law Society.

The dispute originated in July, when the Minister for Justice, Jim O'Callaghan, introduced a uniform flat fee of €520 per case, superseding a structure under which solicitors received €240 for an initial appearance and approximately €60 for each subsequent one. A substantial proportion of practitioners contended that the revised model was financially unsustainable and consequently withdrew their services.

Under the new arrangement, the flat fee is retained; nevertheless, remuneration is now contingent upon the volume and complexity of work. Solicitors will receive €780 where a client faces two separate cases on the same day and €1,040 for three or more, while an enhanced fee of €780 will apply to lengthy proceedings such as domestic violence and custody hearings.

The minister indicated that he was very satisfied that the fundamental reform had been preserved. The president of the Law Society, Martin Lawlor, characterised the negotiations as constructive, maintaining that the agreement addressed the scheme's two most significant deficiencies.

Notably, the High Court had recently ruled that key aspects of the model were grossly unfair and exceeded the minister's legal authority. The judge has postponed her final orders until 24 November, observing that the issue was more appropriately resolved through negotiation.

paragraphs: Criminal defence solicitors are set to resume full legal aid work from Wednesday after the Department of Justice and the Law Society agreed a deal to end a dispute that had lasted more than four months.

The row began on 1 July, when Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan introduced a single flat fee of €520 per case. Under the old scheme, solicitors received €240 for a first court appearance and around €60 for each one after that. Many lawyers argued the new model was unworkable and withdrew their services.

Under the agreement, the flat fee will remain, but enhanced payments will be added. Solicitors will receive €780 when a client faces two separate cases on the same day and €1,040 for three or more. A single enhanced fee of €780 will apply to lengthy cases, including domestic violence and custody hearings.

Mr O'Callaghan said he was very pleased that his reform remained in place. Law Society president Martin Lawlor described the talks as constructive and said the deal resolved the two main flaws in the scheme.

Earlier this month, High Court judge Mary Rose Gearty ruled that key parts of the model were unfair and beyond the minister's powers. She has adjourned her final orders until 24 November, saying the matter was better settled by agreement.
